findings.finding: 'Text in force' still leaves two v4 statements in force that contradict v5. v4 README :505, in the 'W02e K1: boot entries' row, ends: 'Every role and lifecycle capture reports the boot entry it observed (entryId, and SHA-256 of the command line ...), which must be the enrolled one.' v5 captures report no boot entry. v4 README :538 reads: 'The observed hardening.lockdown value, pinned to integrity, remains the evidence of the lockdown state itself.' v5 observes no hardening value; its own lines 140-142 say the hardening settings 'were never observed', and the lockdown state is T04-HOST-LOCKS's. The K1 statement :511-513 says 'The recorded boot entries tell an honest maintenance boot apart'; v4 did that at the data level through the captures' bootEntryObserved (V39, V40), but under v5 only T04-BOOT-ENTRY does. Decision 2's first sentence (:581), 'Boot-entry observation is loader-reported, not measured', has no capture observation left to describe. My round-1 list missed all four.

Name :511-513, narrowed so that only T04-BOOT-ENTRY tells a maintenance boot apart, and :581's first sentence, moot, as :264 already is. findings.finding: check_vectors pins the H ids, their order, their key shapes and the closed set, but not each H case's own content. Swapping H01's and H02's operations was ACCEPTED (284 checks), so H01 'carrying the record's host block' then holds a different boot ID. Changing H18's component from KUBELET to APISERVER was also ACCEPTED. Coverage is not weakened, because the closed set of 22 halves still holds. But the README's per-case table (role or component, intent) could drift from the vectors without check_vectors noticing. The edge record pins the vectors' bytes, so this matters only for a vectors file that check_vectors is meant to vouch for.
findings.requiredChange: Optional: make NEW_CASES carry, per id, its (target, role or component, field, same-value) and require each added row to match. Not blocking.
